verdicts.reason: A uses a coherent two-column banner with readable text, but the headline sits top-right while the dashed dividers frame the body copy in the left column. That splits the reading order, and the headline no longer leads the composition; the left column also floats lower than the headline. B is jumbled: the headline, body and teal line sit on staggered, almost-aligned left edges, and one divider is jammed beside the contact block. The contact lines are shrunk to illegible micro-text, and the top third of the canvas is dead space.
